title: De-axiomatizing the Full Coprime-Consecutive-Divisor Bound τ⊥(n) ≥ ω(n)

problemStatement.formal: \forall n \ge 2,\ \tau^{\perp}(n) \ge \omega(n),\ \text{where } \tau^{\perp}(n) = \#\{\,1 \le i < \tau(n) : \gcd(d_i, d_{i+1}) = 1\,\},\ 1 = d_1 < d_2 < \cdots < d_{\tau(n)} = n,\ \text{proved in Lean 4 without axioms by an injection from the } \omega(n) \text{ prime factors of } n \text{ into the coprime consecutive divisor pairs.}
problemStatement.plain: Write the divisors of n in increasing order and count how many adjacent pairs are coprime; call that τ⊥(n). Erdős observed τ⊥(n) is always at least ω(n), the number of distinct primes dividing n. The parent gallery entry proves only the weak case τ⊥(n) ≥ 1 (the first pair (1, d₂) is coprime for free). This problem asks whether the full bound τ⊥(n) ≥ ω(n) can be machine-verified in Lean by exhibiting one coprime adjacent pair attributable to each distinct prime factor and packaging that as an injection — the parent axiomatizes this bound, noting a formal proof requires intricate reasoning about sorted divisor positions.
whyMatters: De-axiomatizing τ⊥(n) ≥ ω(n) removes a stated assumption from the Erdős #1100 gallery cluster, upgrading the parent toward verified for this foundational Erdős–Hall (1978) bound.

It yields reusable Lean infrastructure about the combinatorics of sorted divisor lists — an underdeveloped corner of Mathlib — and pins down exactly how the 'trivial' bound becomes nontrivial once positions in a globally sorted list must be tracked.

knownResults: τ⊥(n) ≥ 1 for all n ≥ 2 (the ω(n) = 1 case) is fully verified with 0 axioms in erdos-1100-incomplete-01 (theorem tauPerp_ge_one), because d₁ = 1 makes gcd(d₁, d₂) = 1.
The parent erdos-1100 (Erdos1100Problem.lean) states τ⊥(n) ≥ ω(n) as an axiom, alongside the deep Erdős–Hall / Erdős–Simonovits results.
Mathlib provides Nat.primeFactors and Nat.card_primeFactors (ω(n) = |n.primeFactors|), plus Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn for the injection-counting step.
references: P. Erdős, R. R. Hall, 'The propinquity of divisors', Bull. London Math. Soc. 11 (1979) — origin of τ⊥(n) and the ≥ ω(n) bound.
https://erdosproblems.com/1100 — canonical statement of Erdős Problem #1100.
Mathlib.Data.Finset.Sort — Finset.sort, sorted_zero_eq_min', orderIsoOfFin for sorted divisor positions.
